## Task family: solid rectangle + isolated markers, extend the rectangle's rows/columns

Observed in task-a78982e8 (two demonstrations and a correct test answer): input contains a solid rectangular block of color 2, with isolated markers (color 1/3/8) elsewhere. Keep the grid size, original block, and markers. Extend color 2 in straight horizontal/vertical rays from the rectangle, stopping at grid edges, but markers determine which rays/stripes are excluded.

Let the rectangle span rows `r0..r1` and columns `c0..c1`.

- For each row within `r0..r1`, extend the block horizontally to the grid edges. If an isolated marker lies on that row to the left of the rectangle, extend only to the right; if one lies on that row to the right, extend only to the left. With no same-row marker, extend both ways. Do not overwrite markers. (Examples show markers on either side suppress extension toward the marker.)
- For each column within `c0..c1`, extend vertically away from the rectangle on each side. On a given side (above or below), continue a color-2 stripe in every rectangle column except columns containing one or more isolated markers on that side. Markers suppress that column's stripe on the relevant side; other columns extend to the grid edge. Preserve all markers.
- Do not fill the full outside rectangle: the horizontal rays span the rectangle's rows, and the vertical rays span the rectangle's columns, forming a cross-like extension pattern.

The behavior is supported by Demo 2 (5x5 block, row extensions chosen opposite same-row markers; vertical stripes omit columns of markers above/below) and Demo 1. In the solved test, block rows 2–8, columns 9–15; horizontal extensions were row-dependent; downward stripes excluded columns 9, 13, 15 due to markers below, while all columns extended above because no markers were above.
